crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Thematic Coding
children.blurb: Thematic coding is the qualitative research practice of assigning short labels to segments of text, interview transcripts, field notes, open survey answers or documents, so that patterns of meaning can be identified and compared across a corpus.

children.name: Interview Transcription and Speaker Separation
children.blurb: Interview transcription and speaker separation covers the conversion of recorded speech into written text and the labelling of who said what in a multi person conversation.

children.name: Finding Patterns in Lived Experience
children.blurb: Finding Patterns in Lived Experience covers the qualitative and mixed methods work of turning interviews, diaries, focus groups and open survey answers into themes, codes and narratives.

children.name: Ethnographic Synthesis
children.blurb: Ethnographic synthesis is the practice of combining findings from multiple ethnographic or qualitative field studies into a single comparative account.

children.name: Combining Qualitative and Quantitative Data
children.blurb: Combining qualitative and quantitative data is the practice of bringing interview transcripts, field notes, open survey answers and other text or media together with counts, scores and measurements in one study.

sections.body: Qualitative analysis is the work of making sense of interviews, field notes, open ended survey answers and other material that does not arrive as numbers. Artificial intelligence is now used across that work in concrete ways: speech models turn recorded interviews into text and try to label who is speaking, language models suggest codes for passages and group similar passages together, and search and clustering tools help a researcher see themes across hundreds of pages. Ethnographic synthesis, where field notes and documents are read together into an account of a setting, is also being assisted by tools that summarise and cross reference long records. The aim in most of this work is not to replace the researcher's judgement but to remove the mechanical burden of transcription, sorting and retrieval so more time goes to interpretation.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Transcription is the most settled part. Modern speech recognition handles clear audio in major languages well, though accented speech, overlapping talk, poor recordings and technical vocabulary still produce errors that need correction, and speaker separation remains unreliable when voices are similar or people interrupt each other. Coding assistance is genuinely useful for suggesting labels and finding repeated phrases, but models do not know the research question, the theoretical frame or the difference between a theme and a coincidence, so their output is a draft to be checked rather than a result. The harder problems are interpretive: context, irony, silence, what a participant chose not to say, and how meaning shifts across a study. There are also real concerns about consent, confidentiality and where recorded material is processed, and about the risk that fluent summaries flatten disagreement into false consensus. Nothing here removes the need for a human to read the material closely.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages move from raw material to interpretation to integration. Interview Transcription and Speaker Separation covers turning recordings into usable text and the practical limits of doing so, which is where most projects begin. Thematic Coding then deals with attaching labels to passages and building a codebook, and it is the page to read for how AI suggestions fit into an established coding process. Finding Patterns in Lived Experience looks at what emerges when codes are compared across participants, focusing on recurring experience rather than frequency alone. Ethnographic Synthesis widens the frame to field notes, documents and observation, and is the place to go when the study is about a setting rather than a set of interviews. Combining Qualitative and Quantitative Data closes the section by addressing mixed methods, where themes and measurements are brought together, and it is the page for questions about how the two kinds of evidence are joined, sequenced or allowed to disagree.
